Base scheduler steps = total steps. The split-sigmas value = Pass 1 steps (min 6); total minus that = Pass 2 steps (min 4).
E.g. total 12, sigmas 8 → Pass 1 = 8, Pass 2 = 4. Total 10, sigmas 6 → Pass 1 = 6, Pass 2 = 4.

Tip: Pass 1 needs 6+ steps — use 8 for better audio quality.
Mixed-input cap: images + videos + audio combined must total 12 or fewer!
Up to 9 reference images max. Mute (bypass) any LoadImage node you're not using.

The megapixels in the Resolution Examples table are reference values for the Resolution Selector above, not for the Pass 2 scale — you calculate that yourself.
E.g. Pass 1 at 0.5MP (960x544) with a 1.5x Pass 2 scale = 1440x816 output. A 2x scale = 1920x1088.

ULTRA SPEED - Singularity 4-step
=====================================

WHAT CHANGED FROM THE BEST WORKFLOW
  Model  -> Minimax-h3_Singularity_ref2va_v1.3_int8
  LoRA   -> minimax_h3_ref2v_turbo_4step_v0.1
  Sampling -> the Dual Clock node drives it, single pass
  The whole second pass is still here, just bypassed (purple nodes)

  NOTE: Singularity only works with the 4step v0.1 LoRA.
  Do not swap in the 8step one.

SETTING THE STEP COUNT  (this is the only knob - leave resolution at 1.0MP)
  Green Dual Clock node, first field: steps. You never touch a sigma string.

    6 steps   THE DEFAULT. Low-motion shots: talking to camera, walking,
              slow moves. This is the sweet spot of the whole workflow.
    8 steps   High motion: dancing, arms swinging freely, crowds.
    4 steps   Works, but with no margin. It drops words out of spoken
              dialogue when the line is clipped or has weak syllables:
              'Four. Not forty. Four.' lost its 'not' every single time,
              while 'Not forty steps, not twelve - just four.' came out
              clean. Only use 4 if speed matters more than the voice.

  KEEP RESOLUTION AT 1.0MP (1360x768 / 768x1360). That is the LoRA's
  native 768p scale, and what a normal GPU can actually run. Steps buy
  more than pixels: 4 steps at 1.4MP (243s) looked WORSE than 6 steps at
  1.0MP (206s). Spend on steps, not on resolution.

  Timings, a 10s clip at 1.0MP:  4 steps 153s | 6 steps 206s
  Motion is free - a big-motion dance took 205s, the same as a
  locked-off talking head. Only frames x pixels cost anything.

  The sigma curve is NOT a lever. DualClock/beta, DualClock/native_flow
  and a hand-written turbo curve all rendered in ~242s and looked the
  same. Don't waste time there - step count is what moves quality.

WHAT BREAKS AND WHEN
  Ask one question: how much SMALL, FAST-MOVING detail is in frame?

   fine at 4    talking to camera, sitting, walking, slow moves,
                plain or shallow-focus background
   fine at 4    hands resting on knees, gripping a pole, holding a cup -
                anything with a contact point
   needs 6-8    both arms swinging freely in the air
   needs 6-8    busy backgrounds - crowds, traffic, rain, leaves.
                Background pedestrians ghost as they walk away.
   don't bother inversions, flips, dunks - more steps won't fix these

IF THE AUDIO SOUNDS THIN
  Change shift_audio on the Dual Clock node (default 3).
  Do NOT add steps - 4 steps and 8 steps sound identical, the step
  count is not an audio control.
  Audio quality tracks clip length and how much dialogue you write:
  a short clip with one line will always sound hollow.
  Write one line every 2.5s - two lines in a 5s clip, six in a 15s one.

RESOLUTION
  1.0MP is already publishable (768x1360). A 5s talking-head clip
  renders in 76s, a 15s one in 262s.
  The LoRA was trained at 768p,

TURNING THE SECOND PASS BACK ON
  You can (select the purple nodes, press Ctrl+B), but know what it
  gives you: a BIGGER picture, not a SHARPER one. Detail only ever
  carries the resolution it was generated at; upscaling cannot invent
  what was never there.
  Want it sharper? Raise megapixels on the ResolutionSelector instead.

Up to 3 audio refs (must pair with an image or video, 15s total max) — sets pace, dialogue, or ambience.
Up to 3 video refs (2-15s each, 15s total max) — defines camera movement or motion.

nodes.title: * SET YOUR STEPS HERE - Dual Clock (steps / shift_audio)

widgets_values:
[Style] Stylized 3D animated feature film look, soft global illumination, smooth skin shading, no outlines, saturated colors, last dusk light against cool blue shadows, thin translucent energy with clean edges, weighty motion, stable faces, not photorealistic, vertical 9:16 frame.
[References] The woman in @Image1 defines Rumi's identity (face, hair, outfit). The zombies in @Image2 are the shared prototype for the horde: take only their design language (skin, eyes, clothing colors, blank expression) and do not copy the four individuals; every zombie on screen has a different face, hair, build and clothes. The location in @Image3 sets the scene: the layout of the square, the bell tower, iron fence, gate and oak door, and the dusk light. Take only the characters from Image1 and Image2, not their backgrounds; take no characters from Image3.
[Characters]
Rumi: a young woman about 22, one thick long purple braid hanging down her back to the upper thigh, cropped yellow leather jacket with a black lapel collar, white ribbed crop top, dark denim shorts with a red waistband, black lace-up ankle boots; she fights like a kickboxer, fast whipping kicks and knees with tight punches and elbows, and her thin crackling cyan electricity (#5CE1FF) comes only from her fists and palms.
The horde: follows the design language of the four zombies in the reference sheet: dry cracked gray-green skin, cloudy pale gray eyes, blank faces, dusty old everyday clothes in beige, gray and faded blue, every zombie with a different build, face and hair; they shuffle when far away but lunge in sudden, fast bursts when close.
[Entry] Rumi stands in the middle of the square facing the bell tower, the horde surging toward her from every side; the green shelter door is shut.
[Scene] A stone-paved town square at dusk, a band of orange sunset along the horizon under a deep navy sky. In the center stands a five-story stone bell tower; a waist-high black iron fence surrounds its base, and its front door is a thick iron-studded oak door. Far left in the background are the wide steps of the town hall, and beside them a green-painted iron door leads down to an underground shelter. At front right stands an old double-lantern iron street lamp.
[Fight] One continuous shot for all 10 seconds. Her goal is the half-open gate in the fence around the tower: she cuts her way toward screen-right through the zombies in front of her, and the zombies she passes turn and chase her from screen-left. Her tactic: kicks, knees and sweeps stop and break a zombie, and only her electric punch or palm finishes it. At the first frame: the tall zombie in a long beige coat and the bald zombie in a gray vest are in front of her, between her and the tower; the long-haired zombie in a faded blue dress is just behind her. Rumi stays focused and fierce while the zombies pile in harder and harder.
[Motion rules] Rumi fights at full speed from the first frame to the last: every strike snaps out and lands within a fraction of a second, with no wind-up, no pause between strikes, no stance reset, no posing and no teleporting; every burst has a visible plant, travel and re-plant, and every dodge flows straight into the next strike. The tempo keeps accelerating: fast in beats 1–3, faster in beats 4–6, a near-blur flurry in beat 7. Slow motion only for 0.3 seconds on the last punch of beat 7; apart from that one moment, never slow motion.
[Camera rules] Handheld pursuit with a 24mm lens at medium-wide, Rumi's full body and kicks always visible, low angle on every attack. The camera stays on one side of her for the whole clip and never circles around her, so the bell tower always stays on the screen-right side of the frame. The action happens first and the camera reacts a split second late: it overshoots her, whip-pans back along the same side and catches her exactly at each impact, snaps in on the big hits and shakes hard on every contact; ash and zombie bodies wipe past the lens and hide her for a fraction of a second. Never static, never a smooth gliding drift, no face close-ups during the fight, still moving in the final frame.
[Enemy rules] Every zombie on screen is present from the first frame or visibly enters from the screen-left edge; none appears out of nowhere. They attack at the same time Rumi strikes and never wait their turn: one lunges → a second grabs at her braid while she is still turning → a third closes in at the same moment → the ones still standing come back in. They shuffle when far away and lunge in sudden, fast bursts when close. Every zombie reacts only after her strike actually lands; no premature reactions, no fake contact; every hit reads as trajectory → contact → recoil in the direction of the blow → ash from an electric strike, a fall from any other. Once a zombie turns to ash it never reappears; a zombie knocked down without electricity gets back up or is trampled.
[Environment rules] Her boots skid and kick up dust on the stones at every plant; her braid and jacket whip with every burst and turn; struck zombies fly in the direction of the blow and crash into the ones behind them; objects move only when a body actually hits them; no zombie touches Nari.
[00:00–00:01] Beat 1 — FRAME-ONE TEEP, CROSS: Already in motion, facing screen-right toward the tower, she plants and bursts at the tall zombie in a long beige coat lunging at her from in front: teep to its hip, then a crackling straight right into its chest: white flash, it blasts away toward screen-right and bursts into ash. Camera: tight pursuit alongside her, a hard shake on the hit. Sound: a thump, a crack.
[00:01–00:02] Beat 2 — CLINCH KNEES: Without breaking stride the bald zombie in a gray vest steps in front of her; she catches its neck in a Muay Thai clinch, drives knee, knee into its ribs, then snaps a crackling palm strike up under its chin: flash, it bursts into ash. Camera: snaps in on the palm strike. Sound: two crunching thuds, a crack.
[00:02–00:03] Beat 3 — BRAID GRAB FROM BEHIND: From behind her, on screen-left, the long-haired zombie in a faded blue dress grabs her braid and wrenches her head back, teeth snapping an inch from her neck; still facing screen-right, she stamps her heel back hard onto its foot. Camera: jerks in as her head snaps back. Sound: her gasp, teeth clacking, a stamp.
[00:03–00:04] Beat 4 — WRIST DISCHARGE, LOW KICK: Reaching back over her shoulder, she clamps her left palm on its wrist; cyan current races up its arm and it cracks into ash; faster now, she bursts at a zombie in a beige work shirt stepping out in front of her and whips her right shin into its knee, no electricity. Camera: overshoots and whip-pans back along the same side to the kick. Sound: a surge, a thwack.
[00:04–00:05] Beat 5 — LEFT HOOK, GATE AHEAD: Its leg buckles, and as it drops in front of her she snaps a crackling left hook down into its jaw: flash, it bursts into ash; eyes locked on the half-open gate only strides ahead on screen-right, she re-plants and bursts on. Camera: tracking hard alongside her, the tower filling the right of the frame. Sound: a crack, ash bursting, pounding boots.
[00:05–00:06] Beat 6 — LOW SWEEP: A zombie in a faded blue jacket lunges at her from in front, a zombie in a gray hoodie right behind it, blocking the way to the gate; she drops under its arms and sweeps its legs, and it topples back into the hoodie, both crashing onto the stones toward screen-right, no electricity. Camera: drops low with her. Sound: two heavy thuds.
[00:06–00:07] Beat 7 — NEAR-BLUR FLURRY: The two swept zombies rise and two more step in front of her; in a near-blur flurry she fires a crackling jab, cross, left hook and right uppercut, one zombie per punch: flash, into ash; flash, into ash; flash, into ash; flash, into ash, a 0.3-second slow motion on the last. Camera: overshoots and whip-pans back along the same side to each impact. Sound: four cracks in a row.
[00:07–00:08] Beat 8 — TURN TO THE PURSUERS: Instantly full speed: the horde she cut through surges after her from screen-left; she spins around to face it, now facing screen-left with the fence and the tower behind her, and drives a crackling palm into the first pursuer's chest: flash, it blasts away toward screen-left and bursts into ash. Camera: holds its side, snapping in on the palm. Sound: growls, a crack.
[00:08–00:09] Beat 9 — WALL OF HANDS: The rest of the horde slams in from screen-left like a wall of grasping hands; facing it, she side-kicks the next one heel first back into the mass, no electricity, but the crush behind it drives her backward toward screen-right. Camera: medium-wide, handheld, pulled along by the surge. Sound: a thump, a roar of growls.
[00:09–00:10] Beat 10 — SHOVED TO THE FENCE: Still facing screen-left, forearms up, no electricity, she parries and shoves the grasping hands, and the wall shoves her backpedaling toward screen-right until she is a few steps from the iron fence, her back to the tower, the half-open gate within reach beside her but blocked by the crush. Camera: still tracking from the same side. Sound: a stampede of feet, her boots scraping on stone.
[End state] Rumi is being shoved backward by a wall of zombies toward the waist-high iron fence around the bell tower, a few steps from it, her back to the tower, the half-open iron gate within reach beside her.
[Sound rules] Every contact has its own sound: a whoosh before it, a thump or crack on impact, a snarl cut short after it; electricity is a sharp dry crackle and ash a soft hiss, never a magical chime; her breathing and boots run under everything.
[Overall sound] Rapid thumps and thwacks of kicks and knees, sharp electric cracks and ash bursts accelerating into a rattle of cracks, snarls cut short, her gasps and hard breathing, a swelling roar of growls and a stampede of feet, the bell tolling from the tower. No background music, no screaming, no narration.
[Constraints] Characters look at clear objects in the scene, never into the camera. Hard cuts only between shots; no dissolves or fades. No subtitles, captions, text, watermark or logo. Only one of each character, no twins or duplicates. Faces stable, anatomy correct, motion natural and weighty. Electricity appears only where Rumi's fist or palm touches something and travels only along the metal she touches, staying glued to that metal; it never shoots through the air and never forms rings, domes, circles or arcs in the air. Only zombies touched by the electricity crumble into drifting ash, with no blood and no remains; zombies knocked down without electricity get back up or are trampled by the others, and no bodies are ever left lying on the ground. Zombies may grab Rumi's clothes, braid or arms, but they never bite her and their teeth never touch her skin; no zombie ever touches Nari. In this clip there are no cuts at all. Until beat 8 she faces screen-right toward the tower; from beat 8 on she faces screen-left toward the chasing horde, the fence and the tower behind her. Exactly nine zombies turn to ash, each at one strike of her fist or palm; her kicks, knees, stamp, sweep and parries carry no electricity and only set zombies up. Her electricity never touches the fence, the gate or any other metal in this clip. The only zombie that falls and gets back up is the one she side-kicks back into the horde. CRITICAL: 0–7 s she cuts her way toward the tower, accelerating; 7–8 s she turns to face the chasing horde; 8–10 s the horde shoves her back to a few steps from the fence.
[Negative] blood, wounds, severed limbs, corpses, gore, open-mouth close-ups, bent-back joints, face distortion, extra fingers, twins, duplicate characters, subtitles, text, watermark, logo, dissolves, background music, electricity through the air, energy rings or domes in the air, bodies lying on the ground, Rumi falling, Nari hurt, zombies reviving, reversed outcome.
[Fight negative] slow motion beyond the one 0.3-second moment, waiting enemies, enemies taking turns, fake contact, strikes into empty air, enemies falling before the strike lands, enemies appearing from nowhere, teleporting, position skipping, stance reset, posing, floating, static camera, orbiting camera, smooth gliding camera, face close-ups mid-fight
